thread_analysis.thread_summary: Seiko Solutions (Nobuyuki Nakao) requested a quote and clarifications for Bluetooth SIG registration of a Bluetooth V4.2 smart communication unit with an embedded antenna (built around a smart module also carrying LTE/GNSS/WLAN, already certified for Japan's Radio Law/Telecommunications Business Act). The thread covers a five-question clarification round: scope of the RF 2-item test, meaning of the Compliance Folder fee, expected test-to-registration timeline, the actual V4.2 registration deadline (raised both for the current product and a planned future product sharing the same SM-M100 module), and the required physical completeness of the test sample.
all_questions_found: What does the RF 2-item test (¥200,000) consist of, and is real hardware required?
What is the Compliance Folder creation fee, and what does it cover?
What is the expected schedule from sample availability through registration?
By when must we register before the V4.2 deadline — for both the current product and a future product using the same module?
What level of hardware completeness (case, labels) is required for testing?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: RF 2-item test = TP/RCV/CA (receive sensitivity) + TP/TRM/CA (transmit power), requiring a physical test sample. Compliance Folder is the audit-ready document package, retained 1 year post sales-discontinuation. Standard timeline: ~0.5 day test + 1 day report + 3 business days registration. V4.2's actual final registration date is January 31, 2031 (day before Withdrawal Date), much later than the customer's assumed February 2026 Deprecation-related deadline. RF testing requires only mass-production-equivalent RF function, not a cased/labeled unit.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Each answer hinges on distinguishing cosmetic/mechanical completeness from RF-functional completeness, and Deprecation Date from Withdrawal Date — both common points of customer confusion that Allion proactively clarified.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Misunderstanding the V4.2 deadline could cause unnecessary schedule rushing (if assumed too early) or premature project abandonment (if assumed registration was already closed). Misunderstanding test sample completeness requirements could cause unnecessary delays waiting for a fully cased unit.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified — all five clarification points were answered accurately and proactively addressed both the current product and the customer's mentioned future product.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When customers cite a Bluetooth version's deprecation date as a hard deadline, always clarify the Deprecation-vs-Withdrawal distinction and state the actual final registration date explicitly. Also clarify that RF test sample readiness is about functional (not cosmetic) completeness.
